post.summary: Install the default singletons for an organization
post.description: Install every default singleton (dashboard, agent, home, favorites, notifications, context) the organization is missing. Idempotent — defaults that are already installed are left untouched, defaults without an active deployment are skipped, and AI apps are skipped while the organization has AI features disabled. Grants entitlement only; per-resource access is declared through `POST /applications/:applicationId/installations`. Requires a service token. Returns the resulting state of every deployed default, the same shape as `GET /installations/catalog`.

organizationId.description: The organization gaining access to the default singletons

reference.description: Qualified, globally-unique handle: `sanity/<name>` for singletons, `<organizationId>/<name>` otherwise.

installed.description: Whether the organization has an active installation of this singleton.

anyOf.description: An installation linking an organization to a singleton application

unavailableReason.description: Why the organization cannot install this singleton, or `null` if it can. `ai-features-disabled`: an AI app while the organization has AI features turned off. Reported whether or not the singleton is currently installed.

example.message: organizationId is required
Forbidden

post.summary: Reconcile an organization's AI singletons with its AI features status
post.description: Brings the organization's AI singletons (agent, context, persona) in line with its current AI features status, read from the organization. While AI features are disabled, every installed AI singleton is uninstalled and the reason recorded. While enabled, the AI singletons removed that way are reinstalled, along with any missing AI default singleton (agent, context), even one an admin uninstalled; any other AI singleton an admin uninstalled stays uninstalled. Only singletons with an active deployment are reinstalled; one between deployments keeps its reason and is picked up by the next call. Idempotent, so repeated or out-of-order calls converge on the current status. The invariant is reasserted on each call, not enforced against installs that are in flight at the same time; the next status change corrects those. Requires a service token. Returns the resulting state of every deployed AI singleton, the same shape as `POST /installations/defaults`.

organizationId.description: The organization whose AI features status changed

reference.description: Qualified, globally-unique handle: `sanity/<name>` for singletons, `<organizationId>/<name>` otherwise.

installed.description: Whether the organization has an active installation of this singleton.

anyOf.description: An installation linking an organization to a singleton application

unavailableReason.description: Why the organization cannot install this singleton, or `null` if it can. `ai-features-disabled`: an AI app while the organization has AI features turned off. Reported whether or not the singleton is currently installed.

get.summary: List the singleton catalog for an organization
get.description: Report the singletons in the catalog, each with its installation state. A service token sees all of them (media-library, dashboard, workbench, agent, home, favorites, notifications, context, persona); a session token sees only the org-managed ones (context, persona), which is what an organization may turn on itself. Only singletons with an active deployment are returned. `name` narrows to a single singleton and `state` to one side of `installed`. `unavailableReason` says why the organization can't install a singleton (`ai-features-disabled`), or is `null`. post.description:
Deploy a new version to an existing application. The new deployment becomes active, superseding the previous one.
